extraction.name: MathQA
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset of 37k English multiple-choice math word problems covering multiple math domain categories, with fully-specified operational programs. The dataset enhances the AQuA dataset with precise operation-based annotations.
extraction.creator: Aida Amini, Saadia Gabriel, Shanchuan Lin, Rik Koncel-Kedziorski, Yejin Choi, and Hannaneh Hajishirzi
extraction.publisher: University of Washington and Allen Institute for AI
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset uses problems from the existing AQuA dataset and annotates them with formal operation programs through a dynamic crowdsourcing platform. Math problems are first categorized into math domains using term frequencies, then annotators iteratively select operations and arguments until problems are solved. Quality control includes test questions, accuracy thresholds, and validation by multiple validators (at least 2 out of 3 validators must rank the operation program as valid).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of problems from the 2017 AQUA-RAT dataset, which provides over 100K GRE- and GMAT-level math word problems. The problems are multiple choice and come from a wide range of domains. However, there is significant noise in the dataset, including problems with incorrect solutions, problems that are unsolvable without brute-force enumeration of solutions, and rationales that contain few or none of the steps required to solve the corresponding problem.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators sequentially select operations from category-specific lists and corresponding arguments (numbers from problem, constants, or previous calculations) through a dynamic platform. The platform iteratively calculates intermediate results after each operation submission. Programs must include numbers from the problem and produce results close to the correct numeric solution. At least 2 out of 3 validators must rank the operation program as valid for selection. Quality control includes pre-defined test questions with accuracy thresholds; annotators below threshold have their annotations marked as untrusted and re-added to the annotation pool.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Validation accuracy is 94.64% across categories. Expert evaluation of 500 problems shows 92% of annotations are valid. There is 87% agreement between expert validation and crowdsourcing validation task.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 2 out of 3 validators per item for validation
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset contains statistical biases that can be reduced through the use of operation program supervision. The representation language provides an extra layer of supervision that can be used to reduce the influence of statistical bias in datasets like AQuA.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset contains significant noise including problems with incorrect solutions, problems that are unsolvable without brute-force enumeration, and rationales with few or none of the required solution steps. The representation language has limitations in handling complicated or long chains of mathematical reasoning and certain problem types like sequence and high-order polynomial problems.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is suited for training deep-learning models to solve word problems. The representation language and models can be used for math word problem-solving with interpretable operation programs.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Future work plans to extend the representation language and models to cover currently unsolvable problems, including sequence and high-order polynomial problems.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Math problems are first categorized into math domains using term frequencies. These domains are used to prune the search space of possible operations to align with the word problem text. Problems from the AQuA dataset were filtered to remove unsolvable subsets including problems with no words, sequence problems, problems requiring options, non-numeric problems, and duplicates.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Problems from the AQuA dataset were carefully annotated with formal operation programs using crowdsourcing. Problems were categorized into math domains (Geometry, Physics, Probability, Gain-Loss, General, Other) and aligned with operation programs. High-order polynomials and problems where solutions are entirely nonnumeric were omitted. Expert validation showed 92% of annotations are valid with 87% agreement between expert and crowdsourcing validation.
